decisions.reason: Literal Bézier correspondence for the É accent does not change the closing V's construction; the separate lowercase-v extension observation is already represented by its same-message verification.
The exact derivation of the É accent does not alter the architectural construction constraints for the E and L letterforms.
The Hero V terminal supplies the source geometry, but requiring the accent to duplicate that geometry does not modify the approved Hero V itself.

Literal accent-path correspondence does not necessarily change the wordmark's kerning or rhythm requirement; the message's request to begin evaluating spacing is already represented by the existing RESUME.
The accent geometry refinement does not change the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Specifying exact Bézier correspondence for one letterform does not change the final production-ready asset handoff requirement.
The É accent design rule has no effect on the accepted formats for accessible review images.
